newsitem.title: USA: US money managers more cautious on US debt - survey.
newsitem.headline: US money managers more cautious on US debt - survey.

text.p: Portfolio managers turned defensive on U.S. debt markets in the past week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"Money managers appear to have been unnerved by (Federal Reserve Chairman Alan) Greenspan's comments last week and are adopting a more defensive posture," the report said.
Greenspan jolted U.S. markets last week after he wondered aloud about "irrational exhuberance" in U.S. asset markets during a speech last Thursday.

In the week ended December 10, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading rose to 4.97 from 4.89 the prior week; the asset-weighted number rose to 4.68 from 4.64 in the week ended December 3, according to the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 6.47 percent from 6.45 percent.
Duration bogey slipped to 4.21 on an arithmetic basis and 4.91 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Twenty percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 12 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 5.0, up from 4.0 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
